title: Will the National Republican Senatorial Committee report more than $45M in cash on hand at the end of Q3? Above $45M
rules: If the National Republican Senatorial Committee's cash on hand is above $45 million as of September 30, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary: This market resolves based on the official filing data released by the Federal Election Commission (FEC). Only the first official or non-preliminary release of the relevant statistic will be used to resolve the market, and subsequent revisions, corrections, or updates will not affect resolution.

blind.reasoning: The NRSC had a record $48.8M on hand at the end of May 2026. The FEC's committee overview page shows ending cash of about $18.7M for the period through 08/31/2026, so the committee has been spending down heavily ahead of the midterms. Getting back above $45M by September 30 would mean adding about $26M+ net in one heavy-spending month, far beyond its recent monthly fundraising of about $8–10M. The main remaining risk is that I couldn't confirm the $18.7M figure from a second source.
blind.falsifier: The NRSC's October 20 FEC monthly report shows cash on hand above $45M as of September 30, 2026. That could happen through a very large transfer from joint fundraising committees, or because the $18.7M end-of-August figure was wrong.

final.reasoning: The market at about 15% also sees YES as unlikely; the gap likely reflects doubt about the end-of-August figure. If cash really was about $18.7M then, rebuilding to over $45M in one September of heavy spending is very unlikely, so I nudge up to 6% but still bet NO.
